purpose: This repository's own changes to the 7.3 tree. It is applied AFTER kernel-patches/7.3 (cnjn's series), and it only contains changes that were measured on this board - values the vendor's own module and this board's flashed image agree on.

patches.what: The IDM register values this board was measured at: the control word's bit 24 and bit 13, the RX retev threshold at +0x0010, the per-queue routing words, the interrupt mask and the source-to-IRQ routing, the descriptor depth, and the words at +0x0490, +0x2c8, +0x124 and +0xbc. The buffer-pool layout is deliberately NOT here: the 7.3 tree has no jumbo pool, so that part needs a patch of its own.

The RX frame lands 0x80 bytes into the buffer the driver hands to the IDM on this board - run 160 printed a whole ARP request and a whole IP/UDP frame at buffer + 0x80 while the driver looked at the head of the page. Four places move together: the page pool's .offset (which is what the cache invalidation and the device-side sync are taken from), the frame's data pointer, the XDP buffer, and the AF_XDP pool size check. The offset is a read-only module parameter so that one boot with zx279133.rx_frame_offset=0 can settle it on the hardware.

IDM+0x100 takes the buffer count encoded, not the count: the vendor's idm_new_bp_update() writes one 0x400 pulse per 1024 buffers and then the remainders. The 7.3 tree writes the count itself and posts 2048 buffers at start-up, which is exactly a multiple of 1024 - so the hardware is told the pool is empty at every boot. The 7.3 tree has a single pool, so only the vendor's normal-pool field is written.

The LAN service grows a control transaction, which is what the 9132 switch driver needs: a control sequence restores the XMAC image and then the XPCS image, and the XPCS restore takes the XMAC lock itself, so the transaction cannot be the XMAC lock. The patch adds the second mutex (lan_control_lock), the two service operations (control_begin and control_end), the parent's implementation of them, the Kconfig entry for the 9132 switch driver and the Makefile line that builds it.

The XG-PON activation glue and the OMCI transport get their four hooks in the 7.3 tree. The optical RX signal detect is a GPIO on this board and the 7.3 tree's main.c had no GPIO at all, so the patch adds the work that polls it, the loss-of-signal LED trigger the board device tree names, the attach and the stop around the WAN netdev, the carrier kick in the link-up path, and the management queue's prepare in the transmit path. The tree's struct zx279133_eth grows the fields these need, and the three new objects join the NPU module.

The 9132 switch chip's own programming, moved from the 6.18 generation's np.c word for word: the per-port words, the flood groups, the CPU path, the outport map, the isolation matrix, the protocol action table and the PHY enable. The 7.3 tree had the chip's DSA front end and none of this, so the four jacks and the 2.5G port were registered and never configured. The patch also adds the ERAM table bookkeeping the switch tables need - the SE allocator hands the blocks out in order, so a table's base is not a constant - and records the descriptors where the allocation happens. The IDM's source port is the 9132's PPU number, so the PPU is mapped onto the transport VID range, and the transmit drain reclaims the OMCI management queue that shares the ring.

The TX fault isolation model of the 6.18 generation, moved into the 7.3 tree. The tree believed the TX completion counter: an impossible delta was clamped to the number of pending frames and the slots were freed, which releases a buffer the DMA may still own. The ring is now quarantined instead, both logical TX devices are stopped, and a recovery worker flushes the ring, reclaims it and restarts the shared datapath at most once per real completion - a watchdog that keeps firing must not become a reset loop. A datapath that cannot be brought back up is marked failed and the next user restores it.

The RX delivery path of the 6.18 generation, moved into the 7.3 tree. The tree rewrote the L2 header on every frame of the CPU's LAN queues, including the frames that carry an Ethernet type field: that shifts the IP header four bytes to the right and drops every IPv4 and IPv6 frame for a total length of 0x0800. The rewrite is now guarded by a test for the type field. Three places that read past the end of what they had are fixed as well - the ARP branch of the rewrite, the delivery path's read of the frame as an Ethernet header, and the frame an XDP program may have moved. A frame is no longer handed up as CHECKSUM_UNNECESSARY on the strength of the PPU's parsed flag, which says the packet was taken apart and not that its checksum was verified. And a buffer is now handed back to the hardware with the whole window it writes into synchronised, because the IDM is not coherent with the CPU's cache. The 6.18 generation's own page pool layout is left alone: each tree's CPU-side synchronisation is written for its own offset, and moving one without the other would offset the frame twice.
